entries._review_loop: Awareness schedules existing cortex and review helpers. Tool actions retain their own gates; this coarse graph merges function names.
entries.tick: Cortex only auto-dispatches its read-only allowlist; confirm-tier actions are persisted for authenticated owner approval.
entries.check: Guardian observes decision moments and requests model advice; name-based check collisions over-report unrelated tool paths.
entries.consolidate_if_due: Scheduled consolidation can refine skills, stage proposals and write Apex memory reports.
entries.refine_skills: Reflection proposes generated skill rewrites with _trigger=reflection; approval precedes installation.
entries.propose: Initiative gathers evidence and stages goal proposals; approval creates goals.
entries.run_skill: Installed skills are trusted executable code and run on the host. This entry is an inventory boundary, not a sandbox guarantee.

edges.disposition: Shared provider completions use durable budget reservations and usage accounting. The name-based graph is not a complete inventory of paid APIs or proof of a provider billing cap.

Reflection passes a non-manual trigger to create_skill, which stages executable code through approvals. Validation parses without executing generated code. Trusted manual skill installation remains a separate host boundary.
Existing notifications use restraint and source-specific cooldowns; Cortex confirmation notifications request approval rather than executing the staged action.

Cortex run_python uses sandbox.autonomous_backend and refuses without Docker; confirm-tier bash requires approval and dispatcher safety. Installed skills can use the configured host backend; not every coarse path is sandboxed.
Initiative only stages proposals; approvals._apply creates the proposed goal after approval. This is not a claim that every trusted installed skill is incapable of calling goals.set_goal directly.
Reaching stage creates a pending item for approval; staging does not execute the proposed capability.
Existing reports and notes write files. This graph does not prove path confinement; destructive tools retain dispatcher safety and staged writes retain their approval settings.
